newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain truckers, farmers block border with France.
newsitem.headline: Spain truckers, farmers block border with France.

text.p: Hundreds of Spanish truck drivers and farmers blockaded the French border on Friday to protest against violent attacks by their French counterparts on their trucks and produce, union officials said.
The protestors blocked the major crossing at La Jonquera, stopping vehicles from passing the highway toll.
Meanwhile French foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt condemned violence perpetrated by his country's farmers and called for a police report on the incidents.

Spanish farmers' union COAG insisted the protest would remain peaceful and was aimed at drawing attention of the new French government to the aggressive behaviour of French truckers and farmers towards their Spanish neighbours.

"We have suffered extreme aggression from the French toward our drivers, goods and warehouses for many years and we simply ask that the single market principle be respected," Miguel Lopez, COAG's general coordinator, told Reuters from the border.
COAG said close to 1,000 protestors had gathered at the crossing while media reports put the figure at about 500.
Spain's agriculture ministry said it did not support the action and instead favoured talks.

"This action just weakens the negotiating position of the Spanish government which believes that this is not a bilateral problem between France and Spain, but a European Union problem," Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio told local radio.
In Paris, Rummelhardt praised Madrid for condemning the Spanish protestors' tactics.
"We can only welcome the Spanish government's position and reiterate its calls for calm," Rummelhardt told a news briefing.
COAG said protestors relaxed the blockade at noon (1000 GMT) for about 30 minutes to allow some vehicles through.
Last week Spanish farmers gathered at the French embassy in Madrid, throwing tomatoes in protest at French drivers' behaviour.
